comments.author: aloisklink
comments.body:
I agree with @sidharthv96 about the order of precedence.

This PR currently does:

1. Default values defined in `pieDb.ts`
2. Then the `getConfig()` from `packages/mermaid/src/config.ts`, which consists of:
    1. Global defaultConfig (defined in `packages/mermaid/src/defaultConfig.ts`)
    2. Global config (defined by `getSiteConfig()`)
    3. Directive/local config (defined in https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid/blob/99978da55b5a3c383272343c4c92bb1d42cc8cbf/packages/mermaid/src/config.ts#L12)

This seems fine to me!

> How do we get directives so we could assign it?

The `MermaidConfig` defined by directives should automatically be returned by `getConfig()` in `packages/mermaid/src/config.ts` (it will also automatically take care of global defaults/global site config).

---

> What about title? Should directive/yaml override the one in diagram? If so, then current approach isn't doing so:

I think this is an edge case we don't need to worry about. Personally, I feel like the one defined in the JISON should override the one defined in the YAML, but it could go both ways. It's not really too big of a deal, since it should be pretty obvious to somebody that's writing a mermaid diagram that they have two titles in the definition.

comments.author: Yokozuna59
comments.body:
> Personally, I feel like the one defined in the JISON should override the one defined in the YAML

So am I, I think the metadata defined in actual diagram should override the one YAML.

comments.author: aloisklink
comments.body:
> But I'm not sure why we're returning config from current global config.

In the `packages/mermaid/src/config.ts` file, the `getSiteConfig()` returns:
  - The defaultConfig, merged with
  - the global site config (e.g. set by `mermaid.initialize()`)

In the `packages/mermaid/src/config.ts` file, the `getConfig()` returns the diagram specific config, e.g.:
  - The defaultConfig, merged with
  - the global site config (e.g. set by `mermaid.initialize()`)
  - **the diagram specific config (e.g. set by directives like `%%{init: {"flowchart": {"defaultRenderer": "elk"}} }%%`**

I know it's a bit confusing, but even though `getConfig()` in `packages/mermaid/src/config.ts` is globally available, because it's reset in-between diagram renders, and Mermaid renders each diagram sequentially, it actually contains the diagram-specific config that is set in `%%{init:` directives (and maybe YAML directives once we get it set up).

It's definitely worth changing in a future PR, though, since I know the behavior is pretty weird, and it causes bugs like https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid/issues/4345

---

> We can change the `defaultConfig` type into `RequiredDeep` without errors

It's probably best not to do that, since it's not actually correct, since other variables are `undefined`.

Maybe something like `MermaidConfig & {pie: Required<MermaidConfig["pie"]>}` could work, if we know that all values in the pie chart are defined by default?

comments.author: aloisklink
comments.body:
> `optional` attributes defined, and I saw that `Required` ...

This probably won't work for all diagram configs.

The issue is that a bunch of `MermaidConfig` values are "required" (and are set to default values), but some values are truly optional (they're set to `undefined` by default). This means that `DeepRequired<MermaidConfig>` is invalid.

My feeling is that we should probably change the `MermaidConfig` typescript type to have all "required" values (with default values) as required in TypeScript.

Then we can change the `mermaidAPI.setConfig()` function to accept something like `DeepPartial<MermaidConfig>`. But that would be a breaking change, so it's something that will need to wait for v11 (see discussion at https://github.com/orgs/mermaid-js/discussions/4710#discussioncomment-6709156)

> Should we use the diagram's config in API (`mermaidAPI.getConfig` and `mermaidAPI.setConfig` ...etc) in this PR, or leave for future PRs?

Definitely in future PRs :)

It's good practice to keep each PR as small as possible, especially for something like this config file, which is used by every Mermaid diagram.
